title: Glazing Quoting Software | Send Professional Glass Quotes | Coglass
description: Create and send professional glass quotes in seconds. Multiple variants, PDF output, online customer acceptance — all built into Coglass glazing software.
lead: Stop retyping quotes in Word. Coglass builds the quote straight from the glass spec and prices it the way glaziers actually price — variants, trade rates, labour and energy — then sends a branded PDF the customer accepts online with one tap.
steps_h2: From enquiry to accepted quote — without the paperwork
steps_sub: Coglass handles every step of the quoting process. Here's exactly how it works.
inc_h2: Everything you need to quote faster and win more jobs
inc_sub: Every quoting feature is on every plan.
steps: Customers submit enquiries via the embedded web form on your website, or your team creates an order directly in Coglass. Customer name, address, contact details and job description are all captured.
Add each pane to the quote: dimensions (width × height in mm), quantity, product type (cut size, DGU, toughened, laminated), and any operations like polished edges, cutouts or Georgian bars.
Coglass calculates the price based on square metre rates or unit pricing from your product catalogue. Labour and installation charges are added automatically from your settings, or adjusted per job.
Press Send quote, check the preview and send it by email or text. The customer gets the PDF, a link to view and accept it online with no login, or both.
The customer accepts on their quote page and your team is notified. If you ask for a deposit, the job waits for it before going to order. Customers can also decline, with a reason.
The accepted job keeps every glass specification, ready for supplier ordering, production and scheduling — nothing re-typed.
included: Branded PDF quotes
Your company name, logo and colours on every quote.
Multiple quote variants
Send two or three options in the same quote — e.g. standard vs Low-E glass — and let the customer choose.
Online customer acceptance
No printing, no signing, no scanning. Customers accept the quote from a link on their phone.
Auto price calculation
Square metre and unit pricing calculated from your product catalogue the moment you select a product.
Labour and installation costs
Add labour rates and fitting charges automatically, or override per job.
Trade price lists
Per-customer and per-type price lists with discounts and quantity breaks, applied automatically. Prices freeze when the quote is sent.
Quote notes
Add internal notes for your team and visible notes that appear on the customer's quote PDF.
Quote status
See every quote as draft, sent, accepted or declined.
Full glass specification
DGU, TGU, toughened, laminated, Low-E, Georgian bars, lead, cutouts, polished edges — all on the quote.
Embedded enquiry form
Add a glass enquiry form to your own website. Customer enquiries land directly in Coglass ready to quote.
VAT and GST handling
Prices shown before and after tax. VAT or GST calculated automatically based on your registration settings.
No re-keying
The quote is already the order — once accepted, its glass specs carry straight through to production.

stories.label: Quoting real jobs
stories.h2: For the jobs that don’t go to plan
stories.sub: Customers send photos instead of sizes, want two prices for one house, and change the job after the survey. Coglass handles each without starting again.

items.title: A price from their photos
items.problem: The customer wants a rough price before you drive out to measure, but a normal quote commits you to sizes you have only guessed.
items.fix: Send it as a Provisional quote. The customer can say “yes, come and measure”, but no glass is ordered and no deposit is asked for until the real quote, with measured sizes, goes out after the survey.
see: “From their photos — final price after we measure” on what the customer receives
The job moves to Provisional quote accepted, ready to book the survey

items.title: Separate quotes for one job
items.problem: The landlord wants the front and back of the house priced separately, and you end up keeping two copies of the same order.
items.fix: Press Split into separate quotes on the work bench and drag each pane into a section. Coglass offers a quote for each section next to one for the whole job.
see: Quote A for the complete job, plus sections B, C and so on
Accept the whole job or the sections — whichever isn’t chosen shows as superseded
Each section invoiced on its own

items.title: Scaffold charged once, not per pane
items.problem: Tag scaffold on ten panes and it gets charged ten times — so you take it off and add it by hand, and sometimes forget.
items.fix: Set up scaffold, a MEWP or other access as shared hire with a day rate. However many panes need it, the job gets one Access & hire charge: day rate × days.
see: One Access & hire line on the quote and the quote PDF
The number of days changed on the job when you need to
Raise hire order sends the hire company an order for the days you need

items.title: When the job changes after the quote
items.problem: The survey finds a bigger size or the customer adds a pane, and the invoice no longer matches what they agreed. That is how arguments start.
items.fix: A sent quote keeps its price. Change the job afterwards and Coglass shows what was quoted next to what it comes to now, and offers Send amended quote.
see: The customer sees the reason and each change in plain words, such as “Labour added: 2 hours”, and accepts online
When you invoice a changed job, Coglass asks whether to bill the new amount, send the amended quote first or keep to the quoted price
Every quote version kept on the job

items.title: Trade prices that stay put
items.problem: Each builder account has its own rates, and a price rise shouldn’t move a quote they already have.
items.fix: Give a customer, or a whole customer type, a price list: a discount off everything, fixed rates per product, quantity breaks and contract dates. Quotes keep the prices they were sent at.
see: Test a price: pick a customer and a product and see what they would pay, and which rule set it
Import from PDF reads a price list you already have into the rules, for you to check
